abstract: To address the issues of low shopping efficiency in traditional supermarket shopping models, this article proposes a supermarket intelligent shopping cart design that can improve the shopping experience of today's consumers. This design uses the STM32F103VET6 micro controller as the central processor to receive and process peripheral signals and control peripheral devices. Through the application and coordination of multiple modules, and the use of technologies such as ultrasonic positioning and OpenMV cameras, the intelligent shopping cart has functions such as automatic following, emergency obstacle avoidance, and self-service checkout. Finally, debug the above functions separately, analyze common problems that exist during the debugging process, and propose solutions. The design of this shopping cart not only saves consumers shopping time and improves the shopping experience, but also reduces checkout costs, increases popularity, and obtains more profits for supermarkets, providing a certain reference for future intelligent shopping.

articleTitle: Attention Makes Breast Cancer Segmentation in Ultrasound Image Better
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: According to the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) statistics, starting from the year 2020, breast cancer has officially surpassed lung cancer and becomes the world's leading cancer. Early detection of tumors plays a crucial role in clinical treatment, and ultrasound scanning is a cheap and efficient imaging technique that is widely used. Today, with the development of deep learning, an increasing number of network architectures have demonstrated promising performance in medical image processing, among which UNet stands out as an excellent example. In this paper, we compare the effectiveness of UNet,and UNet with attention mechanism,such as TransUnet and SwinUnet in detecting and segmenting breast cancer lesion area based on ultrasound images. From the experiment, UNet with attention show an excellent performance, especially for the TransUnet, which has the best indicators among all the models.

articleTitle: Research hotspots analysis of Edaravone by PubMed
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective: To understand the research hotspots of Edaravone by PubMed. Methods: With MS Excel, SPSS, Cytoscape software, we took MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) word frequency analysis, clustering analysis, co-word network graph of PubMed papers. Results: By MeSH of 1087 papers analyzed, it shows that the current Edaravone research hotspots had focused on “Antipyrine; Free Radical Scavengers; Neuroprotective Agents; Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis; Brain Ischemia; Reperfusion Injury”, etc, it also suggests that the most importance of which was Antipyrines. Conclusion: With multi-angle analysis of bibliometrics, we understand the outline of research hotspots about Edaravone. It is helpful and time saving for the researcher or doctor to understand the research hotspots in Edaravone.

articleTitle: Exploring the Factors Influencing Online Learning Engagement: A Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The rapid expansion of online learning has broken the limitations of college students' knowledge regarding factors such as distance and environment. This study aims to reveal how variations in two aspects, environment and transaction distance, affect college students' engagement in learning. To comprehensively examine this problem, we meticulously collect and analyze data from 605 mid-career students across 17 universities. Employing the rigorous framework of partial least squares structural equation modeling, we uncover intriguing insights into the intricate interplay of variables. The result underscores the profound influence of the online learning environment on students' engagement, explicitly targeting their study skills engagement and participation. Furthermore, our investigation delves into the concept of transactional distance, a pivotal cornerstone in the realm of online education. This element, characterized by the perceived psychological and communication gap between learners and instructors, emerges as a critical factor. It exerts discernible effects on multiple dimensions of student engagement, including study skills, interactive, and affective engagement. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the evolving landscape of online education, elucidating the factors that significantly shape students' engagement. These findings hold significant implications for educators, policymakers, and institutions striving to enhance the quality and effectiveness of online learning experiences in higher education.

articleTitle: Exploring the Collaborative Education Path of Labor Education and Innovation and Entrepreneurship Education in Computer Majors
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This paper proposes the research on exploring the collaborative education path of labor education and innovation and entrepreneurship education in computer majors. The research method is to design solutions and methods based on the actual situation of the collaborative education path between labor education and innovation and entrepreneurship education. The result is to propose the integration of labor education and innovation and entrepreneurship education in computer majors. It achieves the simultaneous development of the five educations and the continuous cultivation of innovative thinking, and constructs an optimized evaluation system for the cultivation of computer innovation and entrepreneurship education with “Quality+Ability” and “Theory+Behavior”. The conclusion is that it has opened up a new path for the collaborative education of labor education and innovation and entrepreneurship education in computer science.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Quiz Question Performance using Preceding Quiz Activities and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This study explores the relationship between quiz question performance and preceding quiz activities, aiming to predict the former through the lens of diverse machine learning models. Our research explores four distinct approaches, namely Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosted Trees, Extreme Gradient Boosted Trees, and Gaussian Naïve Bayes classifiers. By extracting 76 variables from the LMS log files and employing a dataset comprising the data of 455 students, we conducted an investigation categorizing quiz question performance into two classes: accurately and incorrectly answered. The predictive potential of the selected machine learning models was evaluated through metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and fl-score. Our findings reveal that Logistic Regression and XGBoost achieved the highest prediction accuracy rates of 81.8% and 80.5%, respectively.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models in Education
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have been a hot topic in artificial intelligence research., profoundly impacting many fields., including education. LLMs showcase powerful capabilities in natural language comprehension and generation., demonstrating impressive domain generalization after downstream tasks fine-tuning. Therefore., fine-tuning LLMs have attracted much attention from education., and research on their educational applications has begun to enter the public view. This paper undertook a comprehensive examination and analysis of the fine-tuning LLMs and their potential applications in the field of education. On this basis., we explore the common issues currently encountered in fine-tuning LLMs., considering both the advantages and limitations of fine-tuning LLMs and their potential to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of education. Finally., to help educators make informed decisions and foster innovation in education for the better service of human education., we look into the future trends and applications of fine-tuning LLMs in education.

articleTitle: Perceiving Service Quality from Social Media via Natural Language Processing Model
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The prosperity of social media provides us with a vast repository of knowledge. Mining users' perceptions of a specific service from social media can help service providers improve their service quality and identify potential issues that undermine the quality. However, mining user opinions from social media is still challenging. First, social media data are highly unstructured. Second, a sentence may mention multiple objects with different attitudes. Third, to analyze the factors that impact service qualities, it is critical to identify both mentioned objects and corresponding attitudes towards each of them. To tackle the above obstacles, this paper proposed a novel framework based on natural language processing (NLP). Specifically, our framework can extract fine-grained opinions hidden in each piece of social media data. In this paper, an opinion is a triple consisting of three elements: target, aspect, and sentiment. A sentiment expresses a user's attitude about the service, e.g., positive, negative, or neutral. A target is the element that causes the sentiment, i.e., the reason. An aspect is the class of a target. Based on such triples, users' perceptions of service quality can be measured precisely. To empirically study the effectiveness of our framework, we conduct an experiment with Macau International Airport (MIA) and Twitter. The results demonstrate that our framework can successfully perceive user opinions from social media to help improve the service quality of MIA.

articleTitle: Learning Self-Supervised Vision Transformers from Scratch for Aerial Person Re- Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In recent years, person re-identification (Re-ID) as a widely studied computer vision task, has reached a saturation state under closed-world setting, which encourages researchers to further explore more realistic scenarios. Among them, person Re- Idin aerial imagery is proposed and improved due to its unique practical importance in public security. However, since the aerial person images are taken by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV s), influenced by camera height and angle of view, there are more serious problems such as weak appearance feature and occlusion than ground person images. Most of the current state-of-the-art person Re-ID methods on closed-world datasets are based on local convolution neural network, and hardly works well when applying them to aerial person Re- Idtasks directly. In this paper, we improve the emerging vision transformer (ViT) and apply it to the person Re- Idin aerial imagery. It should be noted that a large amount of data is required to be pretrained for ViTs to achieve competitive performance. Considering the limitations of data, computing power and flexibility in practical scenarios, we improve the pre-training process based on self-supervised learning, and achieve training ViTs from scratch with limited data. Specifically, in pre-training stage, the self-supervised paradigm based on parameter instance discrimination is applied to capture feature alignment and instance similarity, which alleviates the data-hungry of ViTs caused by the lack of inductive bias. Extensive comparative evaluation experiments are conducted on the aerial Re- Iddataset. Our method achieves a Rank-1 accuracy of 65.29% and a mean average precision (mAP) of 57.31%, which proves its effectiveness in aerial person Re-ID tasks.

articleTitle: The Application of Artificial Intelligence Technology in Personalized Teaching of Vocational Education
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This paper aims to explore the development trends of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in personalized teaching within vocational education. The research findings indicate that AI technology can meet students' learning needs and interests through personalized learning and customized learning resource recommendations. Adaptive learning systems can automatically adjust learning content and difficulty based on students' abilities and progress, providing personalized learning support and feedback. Virtual reality and augmented reality technologies offer students rich practical training and immersive learning experiences. The advancements in natural language processing and speech recognition provide intelligent learning interactions and support. Enhanced collaborative and social learning foster cooperation and interaction among students. However, the application of AI technology in vocational education also faces challenges such as data privacy and security, technical feasibility, and acceptability. Therefore, future research and practices need to pay further attention to these issues and seek solutions to ensure the sustainable development and effective implementation of AI technology in vocational education. In conclusion, AI technology holds immense potential for personalized learning and teaching in vocational education, driving the development of more intelligent, personalized, and collaborative learning approaches, enhancing students' learning outcomes and professional competencies, and providing teachers with more opportunities for instructional support and improvement. This is of great significance in cultivating talents who can adapt to future professional demands.

articleTitle: Cultivating Elevated Creativity in Animation Design Courses Through AIGC Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The advancement in the field of AIGC has significantly enhanced the level of automation in interactive animation design and has the potential to disrupt the entire industry model. In the context of this transformative landscape, this study introduces the latest explorations in the integration of AIGC into the teaching model of interactive animation design courses. Throughout the process of creating teaching cases, which encompasses conceiving original works, designing and producing them, and setting student development goals and assessment methods, several changes and innovations were implemented based on the characteristics of AIGC. These adjustments were aimed at enhancing students' understanding and practical application capabilities in the field of interactive animation design. Experimental results from the teaching case demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in stimulating students' learning interests and creativity while improving their skills in interactive animation design. Furthermore, the study summarizes the pros and cons of the teaching case and provides suggestions for improvement and future research directions.

articleTitle: Progress in the Treatment of Gastric Cancer by Traditional Chinese Medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective: To explore the clinical efficacy of traditional Chinese medicine in the treatment of precancerous lesions of gastric cancer, gastric cancer and postoperative quality of life, symptoms, signs and indicators. Methods: Relevant clinical studies on gastric cancer in the past 10 years were retrieved from CNKI and Wanfang domestic literature database, and the efficacy and feasibility of traditional Chinese medicine in the treatment of gastric cancer were analyzed. Result:Traditional Chinese medicine in the treatment of patients with precancerous lesions of gastric cancer, gastric cancer and postoperative gastric cancer can not only control symptoms, improve the quality of life, and relieve the suffering of patients, but also achieve the treatment strategy of “prevention before disease, prevention of disease changes, and prevention of relapse after disease”. Conclusion: Traditional Chinese medicine has a good effect on the quality of life, symptoms, signs and indicators of patients with gastric cancer before and after gastric cancer, and provides a clinical reference for the treatment of gastric cancer with traditional Chinese medicine.

articleTitle: Application Research of Large Language Models in Medicine: Status, Problems, and Future
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This article reviews the research and application development of large language models (LLMs) in the medical field, as well as the challenges and opportunities they face. The article first introduces the basic concepts, development history, and key technologies of LLMs. Then, the article takes ChatGPT as an example, and summarizes the applications of LLMs in clinical fields such as clinical consultation, clinical history collection and medical documentation generation, clinical decision support, medical education, etc., and presents some cases to demonstrate the impressive but mixed results of LLMs in the medical field. Finally, the article discusses the future application prospects and challenges of LLMs in terms of interpretability, reliability, privacy protection, ethics, etc., and gives some suggestions for coping. LLMs have the potential to comprehensively reshape clinical medical technology development, and although they face many challenges, they will ultimately benefit patients and practitioners.

articleTitle: Semantic Correspondence with Peripheral Position Coding
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Establishing dense correspondences between semantically similar images is a challenging task. Cost aggregation is a crucial step in finding correct dense correspondences, with the goal of optimizing the initial correlation map thereby removing the ambiguity of the correspondences. Current approaches use transformer architectures for cost aggregation, which lack local priors to adequately capture the local information contained in the correlation map. We propose to incorporate peripheral position coding into the transformer to explore the local information to obtain the matching set and call it the Peripheral Transformer Matcher (PTM). This coding technique partitions the overall receptive field of the self-attention mechanism into diverse peripheral regions, each with its own set of weights. By doing this, the proposed PTM gets a specific local prior by adding an inductive bias to the transformer models and making the initial correlation map less confusing. In addition, a local self-attention module is used to enhance the image features and obtain an enhanced initial correlation map. Comparisons of the experimental results with baselines on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed PTM.

articleTitle: Two-Layer Optimization Scheduling Algorithm for ICU Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) is an important medical treatment unit in hospitals. Effectively scheduling ICU resources, including beds, doctors, and nurses, is not only critical to improving the quality of medical care, but also reduces the workload and improves the quality of care for medical staff. The overall goal of ICU resource scheduling is to minimize medical costs while maximizing medical efficiency. Scheduling of nursing and equipment resources is the most critical and routine scheduling task in the ICU, and the results of these two scheduling tasks affect each other and cannot be completed at the same level of scheduling. Therefore, this article proposes an algorithm for solving the ICU resource scheduling problem using a two-layer model. The basic idea of this method is to determine the number of nurse resources in the ICU in the upper layer, and to find the shortest time for treating patients in the lower layer. The upper and lower layers of the two-layer model interact with each other, and the cost feedback corresponding to the lower layer scheduling will be given to the upper layer, which will then adjust the number of nurse resources accordingly. By using total cost and treatment time as the objective functions for the upper and lower layers respectively, the influence of weights on the scheduling results is avoided. In addition, machine learning models are combined to improve the efficiency of resource scheduling.

articleTitle: Research on Library Smart Reference Services Model Driven by Associated Data
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The widespread application of data and information technology has prompted the transformation and upgrading of library reference service models, therefore to construct a smart reference service model from associated data-driven perspective helps promote the implementation of smart services in libraries. On the basis of elaborating the correlation of associated data technology and smart reference services, the study constructs a smart reference services model that includes intelligent perception of user demand, smart Q&A services, and user intelligent push services. Finally, the study proposes implementation strategies and suggestions for the smart reference service model in order to provide inspiration and reference for the transformation and upgrading of library reference services in big data environment.

articleTitle: Exploration and Assessment of Critical Covariates of Breast Cancer Outcomes via Between-Group Test of Survival Rates at Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Breast cancer, being the most pervasive malignancy globally, poses a substantial threat to the well-being of the female population. Given the pronounced heterogeneity in survival times among affected individuals, a comprehensive examination of the factors governing treatment outcomes becomes imperative. Leveraging a sizable dataset comprising 2,757 breast cancer patients from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, the current study endeavors to assess the foremost covariates influencing the survival outcomes in breast cancer through survival analysis. The analytical framework commences with the application of Kendall analysis to effectuate dimensionality reduction on the dataset. Subsequently, an overarching survival analysis encompassing the pertinent factors is carried out, followed by a series of individual factor-specific survival assessments. Lastly, the results are visualised and discussed. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the crucial covariates by employing a between-group test of survival rates.

articleTitle: cDNA Microarray Image Segmentation Based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Image segmentation is a crucial step for microarray image processing. Due to the diversity of microarray image quality, current unsupervised and supervised methods can't obtain better results on all datasets. To avoid the invalid pixel segmentation aroused by data dimension reduction, this paper proposes an improved deep convolutional neural network (IDCNN). To ensure the size consistency between the input and output images, an end-to-end network model is built and a padding operation is introduced on input spot block images. Meanwhile, an average sampling operation is defined to replace the fully connection layer for enhancing the uniformity between the feature plane and classification result. At last, a simulation dataset and three real datasets are prepared to conduct intensive comparative experiments with KM, FLICM and SVM. Segmentation results on simulation images prove that the average accuracy of IDCNN is a bit higher than SVM, 10 percent higher than FLICM, and about 20 percent higher than KM.

articleTitle: Bioinformatics and Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking-Based Exploration of the Key Targets and Potential Mechanisms of Action of Leucaena Leucocephala-Kawabata for the Treatment of Neocoronaryngitis Elegans
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore the key targets and potential mechanisms of action of C. alba and C. glabra in the treatment of C. neoformans through bioinformatics, network pharmacology and molecular docking, and to elucidate the main targets and signaling pathways that produce therapeutic effects. METHODS: The dataset GSE164805 was obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, and the limma R package was used to search for differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between normal patient samples and COVID-19 patient samples, and the DEGs were subjected to gene ontology (GO) functional enrichment analysis and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) signaling pathway enrichment. The DEGs were analyzed, and the DEGs were combined with drug targets and imported into the Gene/Protein Interaction Search Tool String database to form a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network. The PPI network was screened for functional modules using Cytoscope software, and the genes with the top 5 Degree values were defined as core genes. Subsequently, immune cell infiltration analysis was performed on the disease dataset to explore immune cell infiltration in COVID-19 patients. Finally, MOE software was applied to complete molecular docking. RESULTS: Based on the dataset GSE164805, 4651 differentially expressed genes were obtained from the screening, and Luteinum vulgare contained 20 active components and 13 active components of Chuanbeimu, which corresponded to 652 targets, and 103 potential targets of action. protein interaction network analysis showed that SRC, PTGS2, NFKBIA, CDC42, and IGF1R were the core targets, and drug-target-constituent-disease network analysis showed Luteanin, Berberine, (S)-Canadine as core compounds. Immune cell infiltration results showed that Plasma cells, T cells and other immune cells were highly expressed in COVID-19 patient samples, and T cells CD8 and other places. The molecular docking results showed that the core protein showed good binding ability (binding energy <-5.5 kcal-mol-1) with the core compounds. CONCLUSION: The active ingredient targets and pathways of action in C. alba and C. kawakawa showed significant enrichment in counteracting inflammatory responses and reversing airway remodeling, which is consistent with the mechanism of action for the treatment of neocoronary pneumonia, and has a promising prospect for development in the prevention and treatment of neocoronary pneumonia.

articleTitle: Record and Suggestions on Teaching Supervision for Master's Students─Take Guangxi University of Science and Technology as an Example
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In order to better improve the quality of postgraduate education, Guangxi University of Science and Technology established a postgraduate education and teaching supervision group in 2020. The three-year supervision work has effectively promoted the improvement of graduate course teaching quality and teaching management level, playing a good role in ‘supervision’ and ‘guidance’. However, there are also issues that need to be further addressed, such as the unsatisfactory expected effect of supervision, especially the lack of educational and teaching courses for supervising graduate students' mental health. Therefore, in the future, it is necessary to continuously explore and innovate the content and methods of graduate teaching supervision, better serve graduate education and teaching work, and improve the quality of supervision.

articleTitle: Application Oriented Undergraduate School - Enterprise Cooperation and Informationization Construction Based on Customer Relationship Management Ideas
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In order to make the cooperation between industry and school in applied undergraduate colleges more scientific, this article proposes a method of industry school cooperation based on customer relationship management. This method analyzes the organizational structure, evaluation system, customer communication and other difficulties using ideas such as customer segmentation, customer value theory, relationship marketing theory, informatization, and socialization. Finally, the informationization construction was carried out based on the cooperation between F College and the enterprise. The research results indicate that this method effectively promotes the development of school enterprise cooperation.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Sentiment Analysis Model of Students by Fusing Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: By recognizing students' facial expressions in a classroom, it is possible to determine in real-time whether students are confused, dissatisfied or happy. Understanding students' emotional states helps teachers adjust teaching strategies and methods, thus improving the quality and effect of teaching. However, classroom scenarios are often complex, and most previous expression recognition methods suffer from the problems of missing local features and low accuracy. Additionally, the imbalanced distribution of datasets has an impact on the recognition accuracy during model training. Therefore, in this paper, based on deep learning theory, an LCANet model, which incorporates an attention mechanism, is proposed to realize the recognition and analysis of students' expressions during classroom teaching. To optimize the global feature extraction capability of the network, the model uses ConvNeXt V2 as the backbone. Moreover, to enable the model to better focus on the important parts of facial expressions, we add an improved channel space attention (CSA) module to extract local features. In addition, we introduce the LF loss function to alleviate the class imbalance problem in the facial expression dataset. The experimental results show that our LCANet model achieves good recognition rate on the public FERPlus dataset with 91.43% accuracy. Therefore, the proposed LCANet model has good robustness and expression recognition performance.

articleTitle: Reho Analysis of the Cerebral Functional Effects of Jin's Three Needle Combined Mirror Therapy-for Patients with Ischemic Stroke
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: This study investigated the effects of Jin's three needles (JTN) combined with Mirror Therapy (MT) on brain function in patients with upper limb dysfunction in ischemic stroke and the possible mechanisms of central effects by using fMRI technique. Methods: Forty patients who met the study criteria were divided into treatment group (JTN+MT) and control group (JTN) by randomized numerical method. The control group was given Jin's three-needle therapy, while the treatment group was treated with mirror therapy for 30 min on top of the control group for 5 days per week for 4 weeks. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance (fMRI) scanning BOLD brain functional image acquisition was performed before and after treatment. The differences in local coherence (ReHo) between the two groups of patients before and after treatment were analyzed and statistically analyzed. The Fugel-Meyer Motor Function Upper Extremity Element (FMA-UE) score, (Mini Mental State Examination, MMSE) score were also utilized to evaluate the two groups of patients before treatment and at the end of the treatment course.Result: After the treatment, the brain regions with significantly increased ReHo values in the treatment group compared to the control group were Corona radiata, Caudate nucleus, Cingulate Gyrus, Supramaginal Gyrus, Inferior Temporary Gyrus, Precentral Gyrus, and Middle Frontal Gyrus (voxel cluster volume>54, P<0.05). In the FMA-UE score and MMSE score, the treatment group was higher than the control group, and the difference was statistically significant (P<0.05).Conclusion: Jin's three needles combined with mirror therapy may promote better activation and reconstruction of relevant brain functional areas (motor, cognitive and memory) in patients with upper limb dysfunction in ischemic stroke.

articleTitle: A Review of Deep Learning Applications in Lesion Detection Research
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: As a powerful machine learning technique, deep learning has been widely applied to lesion detection in medical image processing. This review summarizes the research progress of deep learning applications in lesion detection. Firstly, the characteristics of medical image data are introduced, and the datasets and evaluation metrics of lesion detection are summarized. Then, the main contents of deep learning, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), YOLO algorithm, and SAM, have demonstrated good performance in medical image processing. Meanwhile, the applications of lesion detection in different medical image modalities are discussed, and the advantages of deep learning in different lesion types are highlighted, such as high automation, good performance, and transferability. In addition, some challenges of deep learning in lesion detection are discussed, such as sample scarcity, interpretability, and reliability. Finally, the future development directions of deep learning in lesion detection are discussed, such as multimodal fusion, transfer learning, and labeled data. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the research progress of deep learning in the field of lesion detection, which offers guidance and reference for related research and applications.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Education: Opportunities, Challenges, and Suggestions
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has emerged as a transformative trend, revolutionizing traditional teaching and learning methods. In this paper, we explore the applications and implications of using AI in education. First, it outlines the major opportunities of AI in enhancing teaching and learning, such as providing personalized and adaptive learning, intelligent tutoring systems, and automated assessment. However, AI also brings challenges including high upfront costs, data privacy concerns, and the need to rethink curricula and teacher roles. To maximize the benefits of AI, several recommendations are provided, including developing robust AI systems, creating supportive policies and so on. Overall, AI is a promising innovation which can empower new educational models. We hope this work will draw more attention from interdisciplinary researchers to further develop ethical, transparent and socially responsible AI applications in education.

articleTitle: A Hyperspectral Band Selection Network Combining Siamese Network and Local-Global Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Hyperspectral images can provide dozens to hundreds of continuous spectral bands, greatly enhancing the richness of information. However, the redundancy among adjacent bands leads to increased data processing complexity. Despite the recent introduction of numerous band selection methods, there has been limited focus on incorporating context information from the entire spectral range into this task. Furthermore, researchers have primarily concentrated on band informativeness and sparse representation for reconstructing all bands, often overlooking the separability of classes in downstream tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a hyperspectral band selection network combining Siamese Network Local-Global Attention (SLGA). This approach first segments the hyperspectral image into homogeneous regions and constructs sample pairs based on a random elimination strategy. Next, it utilizes the Local-Global Attention (L-GA) mechanism to obtain band weights that capture both local and global spectral structures. These reweighted bands are then fed into a twin network to obtain their high-dimensional representations, compute loss values, and update network parameters. Finally, extensive classification experiments using SVM, KNN, and LDA classifiers are conducted on the Indian Pines and Botswana hyperspectral image datasets. The results from these experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed SLGA method performs exceptionally well, outperforming state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Grammatical Evolution for Predicting Cervical Cancer Recurrence Risk
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Cervical cancer is one of the most common tumors in women and has a high rate of recurrence after surgery. Early detection of symptoms leading to earlier treatment can significantly reduce the risk of patients. Artificial intelligence assists in diagnosing the recurrence of cervical cancer, which can reduce diagnostic costs and increase early identification of symptoms for timely treatment. In this study, grammatical evolution was used to develop a predictive model. The model included the corresponding grammar, evolutionary strategies and adaptations for common influences and important independent features. The grammatical evolution model was compared to the predictive model constructed using decision tree algorithms. The results show that the predictive model based on grammatical evolution performs well in predicting cervical cancer recurrence. Furthermore, due to the flexibility and adaptability of GE, the model can achieve desirable results by adjusting parameters. The model's efficiency improves when using important independent features obtained from the decision tree algorithm as the grammatical evolution inputs. Then, the importance of all features in the model was determined using the permutation importance. In this proposed model, the key features for predicting recurrence are pathologic T, pathologic stage, LNM, surgical margin involvement, and RT target summary in descending order of importance. These results will help clinicians to pay attention to patients with such risk factors before recurrence occurs.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Main Treatment of Chengshan(BL57) and the Dispensing Pattern Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Based on the study of clinical cases in modern literature, the Chinese periodicals (CNKI), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform (Wanfang) and Wipu Information Chinese Journal Service Platform (VIP) were searched for the relevant literature since the database was established until February 28, 2023. Besides, SPSS Statistics27, SPSS Modeler18.0 statistical software were adopted for the literature on the Chengshan(BL57) manipulation, single-point treatment, acupoint combinations and other related literature for frequency analysis, association rules, cluster analysis. A total of 132 pieces of related literature, including 16 pieces of single-point treatment literature, 116 pieces of literature on the treatment of acu-points; Chengshan(BL57) were mainly used for high-frequency therapeutic manipulation of: acupuncture, acupuncture and cmoxibustion, etc. Among them, single-acupoint treatment for 8 diseases and combined-acupoints treatment for 26 diseases, of which the diseases of the motor system and the anorectal disease system are mostly treated with single-acupoint treatment, such as the dominant disease mainly treating acute lumbar sprains, gastrocnemius muscle spasm, hemorrhoids, etc., with the acupoints also based on the locomotor system, mostly sciatica, lumbar intervertebral disc herniation, hemorrhoid postoperative pain. Most of them belong to bladder meridian of bladder meridian of foot-taiyang(BL), gallbladder meridian of foot-shaoyang(GB), stomach meridian of foot-yangming(ST). Additionally, the high frequency of its combination of its high frequency matching acupoints are: Yanglingquan(GB34), Weizhong(BL40), Huantiao(GB30), Kunlun(BL60) etc.

articleTitle: Tracking and Monitoring Method for Multi-Target Moving Ships Based on High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: To address the problem of ship target probing and detection in vast sea areas, a new method is proposed to realize rapid, positioning identification, and motion tracking of multitarget moving ships by comprehensively utilizing the characteristics and advantages of satellites in orbits of different altitudes. According to the characteristics of ship targets and the prechecking of geostationary orbit satellites, low-earth orbit satellites are deployed to coordinate investigation and capture high-resolution remote sensing images, which can be used to quickly designate target candidate areas, effectively improve the search efficiency, and achieve accurate positioning of ship targets and fine-grained recognition and classification of “Ship-Category-Model”. The DeepSORT algorithm was improved to use a single small neural network structure by adding the functions of speed and course estimation, track plotting, and dynamic management, and it was used to extract the apparent features of ship targets and integrate them with common position information to participate in the inter-frame data association. Through satellite video inspection and simulation experiments, the feasibility and robustness of accurate and stable tracking in remote sensing scenarios and multi-target moving ship tracking and detection tasks were verified by mining and utilizing the advantages of high-resolution images.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Digital Media Course Case Study in an Art University
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: In art universities, digital media general courses for undergraduates have a robust artistic attribute. This paper designs a course case integrating aesthetic education. This case used the scores of a group of short video clips, which participated in a short video competition for college students, as the basis for its data. And it is analyzed through a series of data processing. Comparing the actual ranking of the competition with the way students scored the short video clips while achieving the teaching goals and aesthetic education effects, the analysis result shows that the final result ranking of the competition and the overall rating results given by the students are similar, demonstrating the objectivity and fairness of the competition. However, the differences in details also reveal the inconsistency between the public rating and the expert rating. And all of these indirectly imply the importance of data analysis in real life.

articleTitle: Quality Assessment of Electrocardiogram Signals Using Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Quality assessment of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals holds significant importance in reducing the high-frequency false alarms in automated arrhythmia diagnosis. Existing quality assessment methods primarily rely on empirical threshold setting or the calculation of relevant statistical values to formulate decision rules. However, the thresholds set in this manner are typically based on experience and knowledge, resulting in decision rules that lack flexibility and struggle to adapt to changes in the dataset. To address this issue, many researchers have turned to deep learning algorithms for ECG signal quality assessment. Nevertheless, most existing deep learning methods usually require large-scale and labeled ECG data for training, whose acquiring is typically challenging. Therefore, this paper proposes an efficient method for ECG signal quality assessment. First, we use a contrast learning framework to construct sample pairs through multilevel data augmentation. Second, a densely connected convolutional network (DenseNet) is used to improve the model's ability of extracting local features in ECG signals, and a Squeeze-and-Excitation attention module is introduced to make the model pay more attention to critical features. Finally, the feature representation is learned by minimizing the contextual contrast loss to bring similar samples closer and push dissimilar samples farther away. In this way, we can utilize the contrastive learning framework to extract temporal representations from unlabeled data and transfer them to downstream ECG signal quality assessment tasks. Extensive experiments on the Physionet/CinC Challenge 2011 dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms most existing quality assessment methods.

articleTitle: Clinical Efficacy of Xi San Zang Decoction Concomitant with Musicotherapy in Patients with Knee Osteoarthritis and the Influence on Levels of Related Serum Factors
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Objective: To explore the clinical efficacy of Xi San Zang Decoction concomitant with musicotherapy in patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) due to syndrome of liver and kidney deficiency. Methods: A total of 62 patients with KOA due to syndrome of liver and kidney deficiency were randomized into treatment group and control group based on random number table, 31 cases in each group. Treatment group received oral Xi San Zang Decoction concomitant with musicotherapy (in which 3 music songs with Mi tones and La tones were selected and played circularly in the morning, at noon and at night in quiet environment with doors and windows closed, 20 min per song, with song decibel (DB) controlled <70 (better at 40 to 60), concomitant with Xi San Zang Decoction, decocted by water, 100 mL, bid. Control group received Imrecoxib Tablets 1 tablet per dose, bid. The changes of Lysholm score and VAS score before and after treatment, the clinical efficacy and the changes of levels of related serum factors were compared between two groups. Results: After treatment, Lysholm score and VAS score significantly improved than those before treatment and the clinical efficacy was prominent in both groups, and the differences were statistically significant (P<0.01). Treatment group was superior to control group in the improvement of Lysholm score and VAS score after treatment and was better in clinical efficacy than control group, and the differences were statistically significant (P<0.05). Treatment group was evidently lower in the levels of serum interleukin (IL)-1 and tumour necrosis factor (TNF) -α than control group, and the differences were statistically significant (P<0.05). Conclusion: Xi San Zang Decoction concomitant with musicotherapy has good efficacy in treatment KOA, deserving to be clinically studied and popularized.

articleTitle: Label Semantic Improvement with Graph Convolutional Networks for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Multi-label classification of Chest X-ray images is one of the important tasks in the field of medical image analysis, and current methods only capture co-occurrence relationships between labels, making it difficult to establish complex connections among labels. We face a series of challenges when considering global label correlation, visual correlation, and dealing with unbalanced data. In this study, we introduce a Label Semantic Improvement Graph Convolutional Network (LSI-GCN) framework based on GCN, which consists of an Image Representation Learning module, a GCN module with Label Semantic Improvement, and a Distance Metric module to improve classification performance. The task of multi-label classification of chest X-ray images is approached from different perspectives and levels by combining their functionalities to improve the performance, robustness, and accuracy of the model. The Image Representation Learning module is a feature extractor that learns high-level label-specific features from chest X-ray images. The GCN captures label correlations and models global label relationships and category visual correlations, respectively. With this approach, the correlation between disease labels and the relevance of image features can be considered simultaneously, and the accuracy of multi-label classification can be improved. The image features were further optimized using a distance metric module. Experiments were conducted using Chest X-ray14 and CheXpert images as multi-label datasets, and the mean Area Under Curve (AUC) scores obtained were better than those of comparative models such as CheXGCN [3] and the accuracy and robustness of multi-label classification were improved.

articleTitle: MIE: Main Information Enhanced Network for Few-Shot Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The goal of the few-shot action recognition task is to recognize actions in videos based on limited action category data. The current main method is to perform multilevel matching on the extracted visual features. However, before feature matching, the richness of the extracted feature information can affect the ability of subsequent feature matching. Therefore, in this article, we propose a feature extraction module with subject information enhancement, which can enhance the network's perception of the main characters and objects in the video during the feature extraction stage, thereby improving the ability to obtain video information. At the same time, we have also redesigned the global-local feature matching method so that the extracted video information can be better matched to complete action recognition. We achieve good performance in three benchmark tests, and also provide a new idea for research in this field.

articleTitle: Principles of Diffusion Models and Their Applications on Medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Diffusion models, as a paradigm of generative models, have achieved unprecedented success in the field of image generation since 2020, owing to their advantage of simplicity in optimization. They have been widely applied to various tasks in fields such as image, text, and speech processing. Notably, due to a series of breakthroughs achieved by diffusion models in natural image generation, the field of medical imaging has actively explored the potential of diffusion models. This paper begins with a detailed introduction to the principles of diffusion models. It then categorizes the applications of diffusion models in the field of medical imaging into various tasks, including generation, 3D reconstruction, segmentation, image-to-image translation, and classification, highlighting the main methods for each task. Finally, the paper summarizes the research progress of diffusion models in the field of medical imaging, discusses key challenges and open issues, and proposes promising directions for future improvements.

articleTitle: Identification Method of Alzheimer's Disease Based on Fine-Tuning Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is one of the most well-known irreversible neurodegenerative diseases, which afflicts a large number of people around the world, especially the elderly.It is particularly critical to use simple and quick techniques for early diagnosis of AD. This paper presents a Vision Transformer(ViT) model based on Fine-Tuning for the classification of the degree of AD symptoms.By preprocessing and optimizing the MRI images of AD and a simple and feasible classification problem transformation strategy, the research achieves an accuracy of 0.96219. At the same time, we used several other evaluation metrics and pre-trained models for testing.The results show that our model performs exceptionally well in distinguishing Alzheimer's disease.This study helps to advance the advancement of neuroimaging and clinical diagnostic techniques for AD, and promotes the research of neural networks in the medical field.

articleTitle: Training and Practice of Computational Thinking for New Engineering Subjects
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, the talents of high-quality composite New Engineering Subjects need strong engineering practice ability, innovation ability, and international competitiveness. The college students have not only basic skills in computer operation but also certain programming skills. Those who understand and practice computational thinking will solve various non-universal computing problems encountered in work and study in the contemporary information society. In order to support the teaching objectives and educational concepts of the new engineering discipline, teaching reforms have been carried out in terms of teaching objectives, teaching content, teaching models, teaching resources, and ideological and political education. We cultivate interdisciplinary and professional integration through advanced thinking methods. It integrates knowledge points into practical engineering applications and cultivates students' computational thinking ability. It also improves the practical application and problem-solving abilities of students. In addition, we integrate ideological and political elements into the teaching process. It is a teaching method that combines moral education and professional courses.

articleTitle: Recognizing Crop Diseases and Pests Using an Improved MobileNetV3 Model
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: Crop diseases and pests contribute to reduced crop yields and are often difficult for humans to accurately and quickly identify. The performance of plant pathologists or farmers is heavily reliant on their experience. To address this issue, we propose a crop disease and pest recognition method using a lightweight neural network and transfer learning. First, we analyze the data distribution of the training set and use label shuffling and mixed sampling methods to balance the data. Second, we pretrain MobileNetV3 on the ImageNet dataset and transfer the parameter values to the crop disease and pest recognition model for fine-tuning. Third, we improve the activation function and loss function of MobileNetV3, resulting in the creation of MobileNetV3+. This model uses a 6-level-LeakyReLU activation function to replace the ReLU activation function of MobileNetV3, which reduces the loss of negative feature information in crop pest images and improves feature extraction integrity. Additionally, we use focal loss instead of cross-entropy loss to improve the model's ability to handle imbalanced sample distributions. Finally, we train four models (VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNetV3, and MobileNetV3+) using the same method. Experimental results show that MobileNetV3+ has the best overall pest recognition results. Our proposed method can rapidly recognize crop diseases and pests with significantly fewer model parameters and memory requirements, as experimentally verified.

articleTitle: A Study on the Application of Metaverse in Vocational Education
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The metaverse is a new form of teaching and learning, which points out the way forward and the direction of endeavour for the form of teaching and learning. The superiority of the metaverse has been emphasized in the case of the new pneumonia epidemic. The metaverse brings new life and learning opportunities to teachers, students, businesses and participants. Educational meta-ecology is a driven meta-ecology that is driven by factors such as real needs, market needs, individual needs and macro-environment. It provides an immersive, authentic, interactive, innovative, diversified and synergistic educational meta-ecology for education, which can effectively promote educational teaching, reform and innovation, and better promote the development of education. The era of metaverse requires higher vocational colleges to have an objective cognition of metaverse, and it needs to be applied to empower higher vocational colleges. We should use the educational metaverse to promote the reform of teaching methods in higher vocational colleges and universities, and at the same time, solve the difficulties faced by higher vocational colleges and universities. On this basis, we analyze the potential risks such as privacy risk and addiction risk, and put forward corresponding coping strategies, with a view to providing certain reference significance for the high-quality development of higher education institutions.

articleTitle: The Emotional Design of Online Courses to Promote Learner Engagement
publicationTitle: 2023 13th International Conference on Information Technology in Medicine and Education (ITME)
abstract: The study intended to integrate intelligent technologies to the emotional design of online courses to enhance learner engagement in online education. Guided by Emotional Design Theory, it elaborated the rationale of the emotional design of online courses, and then proposed that with the support of artificial intelligent technologies, the emotional design can be actualized by following the principles of visualization, interactivity and personalization, and applying the strategies of constructing emotional online learning resources, organizing emotionally charged learning activities and managing an emotional online learning environment. It was held that the principles and strategies proposed are able to endow learners with a full range of intelligent emotional companionship and interaction. Conclusively, a tentative operational framework for the emotional design of online courses to promote learner engagement was established, providing a referential approach for the sustainable development of scaled and personalized online education.
